headline: Chip rebound lifts the Nasdaq 0.8% on Election Day as Apple's margin warning drags the Dow
summary: A narrow, split session. The S&P 500 opened higher and held a gain of up to 0.7% before settling up 0.4%, snapping a three-day losing streak, but the move rested on a handful of tech heavyweights: decliners outnumbered advancers in the index by about 1.6 to 1. Money rotated from Apple and defensive sectors into beaten-down chipmakers, with tech up about 1.3% while consumer staples and materials each lost close to 1.8%.
drivers: The SOX rose 2.6%, recovering most of Monday's 3.4% drop, as Nvidia gained about 2.3% after four straight declines and Micron about 2.6%; Microsoft and Amazon each added more than 2%. Strategists described it as a rotation out of 'safe' tech into riskier AI names after the Nasdaq-100 confirmed a correction on Monday.
Apple's memory-cost warning weighs on the Dow

Apple fell about 1.9% after guiding holiday-quarter gross margin to 45–46%, below forecasts, as memory chip prices rise, with Greater China and iPad sales also short of estimates despite a revenue and EPS beat. Palantir slipped on slower US commercial bookings, and Gartner (−13%), Thomson Reuters (−10%) and Shopify (−9%) fell after their reports.

September job openings jumped to 7.52 million against forecasts near 7.1 million, with quits rising, keeping a December Fed hike in play; the 10-year yield climbed about 7bp to roughly 4.97%. Meta's bond sale added to supply pressure on Treasuries.
Midterms and Iran keep traders cautious

Volume ran below average as Americans voted, with polls and prediction markets leaning toward Democrats taking the House. WTI swung between $93.59 and $98.82 on a reported US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island and talk of a draft peace memorandum, settling 0.4% lower at $96.09.
week: Two sessions in, the S&P 500 is down 0.1%, the Nasdaq down 0.3% and the Dow roughly flat; the backdrop is a Fed on hold at 3.75–4% with hike risk back in focus, a 10-year yield near 5% and AI spending worries that have pushed the SOX about 20% below its October high.
watch: Next: after Tuesday's close AMD beat with revenue of $13.4 billion and guided Q4 to about $17 billion, sending the stock up more than 4% after hours; midterm results arrive overnight, then Wednesday brings ADP payrolls, the Treasury refunding and results from Arm and Qualcomm, with the October jobs report on Friday, Nov 6.
